what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed the historic district bylaw (article 26) as amended, after amendments to commission makeup, map wording and review deadlines.
A request to remove one property from the historic district failed.
The Village Center District (article 27) passed as amended, with freestanding signs needing a planning board special permit and the window transparency minimum lowered.
Articles 28 to 36, covering zoning housekeeping, two scenic roads and acceptance of White Tail Crossing as a public way, all passed unanimously.
The article to rezone the Riley Stone parcels to limited business residential was still under discussion when the captions end; no outcome is audible.

why_it_matters: The historic district adds review of changes to properties inside its maps, and the Village Center rules set sign and storefront standards for future development in the center.
The finance committee reported no direct financial impact from the zoning articles, but the rezoning debate turned on costs to one family's property, and its result is not in the minutes.
watch_next: The Village Center bylaw takes effect January 1, 2016, with further public hearings on signs possible before then.
The recorded vote on the Riley Stone rezoning article, which is not audible in these captions.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed the general FY16 operating budget; the minutes record the vote as passed, without a count.
The two-thirds vote on the capital plan passed, funded from reappropriated balances, cash and borrowing for a dump truck and a street sweeper.
A stabilization fund deposit passed unanimously; the minutes say it maintains a five percent reserve.
Sewer, solid waste and water enterprise budgets passed, with no rate increase for sewer and no price change for solid waste bags.
The Article 26 architectural preservation district bylaw was still in debate when the captions end, and the minutes record no vote.

why_it_matters: The operating budget, the capital plan and the start of the middle-high school debt exclusion in FY16 together shape the next tax bill, and sewer and trash rates are unchanged.
If Article 26 is adopted, property owners inside the mapped district would face design review and review deadlines, so the outcome and the map's notice are things to check.
watch_next: The outcome of Article 26, which the captions do not show, including any amendment on review deadlines the moderator asked to be written down.
Any answer from the capital planning chair on town hall next year.
